parsed.explanation: Split combined regime: severe national border/passport, federal facilities and custody exposure remain, while strong state protections lower everyday in-state risk. Adult alone and minor-guardian are Elevated Risk because entry screening can out, strand, or refer into abusive federal custody; shield law and anti-discrimination protect state services and care but not federal.

entry_documents.exposure: National order bars self-selected passport/visa markers; new passports/visas follow birth sex; officers may refuse visas when documents/presentation mismatch and treat wilful misrepresentation as fraud, risking stranding.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid; civil-liberties suit and legal-aid guidance; state M/F/X IDs help after entry but do not override border/visa rules.
entry_documents.interaction: Mismatch can trigger secondary screening, denial, removal, and immigration custody; state non-discrimination does not shield entry adjudication.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary, sexual abuse; federal corrections adopts conversion-therapy policies and hormone removal; entry denial can lead to detention.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: State custody policy treats detained people by gender identity in strip/housing; shield law protects care-seeking.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: State protections do not cover federal immigration/national corrections; federal custody exposure can follow border referral despite protective state.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National order bars government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity; several states ban or criminalize; federal facilities in this state likely enforce.
federal_state_facilities.protection: State public-accommodation law prohibits identity discrimination; Most Protective tier and no documented state bathroom ban.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Private/state facilities may be protective, but federal/funded facilities and immigration housing can still exclude or place by birth sex.

care_services.exposure: National minors-care orders, school investigation threats, funding freeze, proposed reimbursement bans, and record subpoenas restrict care access.
care_services.protection: State shield law protects patients/providers from home-state charges; anti-discrimination; conversion ban; sports protections.
care_services.interaction: Visiting family can use state care, but federal school/funding actions may chill providers and expose minors.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Counterterrorism names 'radically pro-transgender'; national directives investigate schools/prosecute teachers; federal funding and enforcement frame care as hostile.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime law, employment ruling; state hate-crime law strengthened, anti-discrimination, gay-panic repeal.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State actors may protect; federal actors can investigate/freeze schools and providers, especially after document mismatch.

minors_guardians.exposure: National regime criminalizes/prosecutes social transition and funds school investigations; parent/minor travel may be questioned and care access chilled.
minors_guardians.protection: Shield law, anti-bullying, conversion ban, athlete eligibility, custody policy protect minors and guardians.
minors_guardians.interaction: Care-seeking minor is safer state-side; guardian's entry/federal care still exposed; home-state bans do not control state care.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state violence count; national polls and hostility may increase misgendering, refusal, or police interest.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State anti-discrimination/hate-crime and gay-panic repeal; local police may be more respectful, not evidenced.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Street risk likely lower than national average; remedies exist but enforcement incidents unquantified.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Orders contested; several enjoined; timing/agency/federal-state boundary changes outcome; no state incident or homicide baseline.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts, civil-liberties suit, legal FAQ, shield law and state remedies may help; no documented federal relief.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Protections are robust in state but uncertain against federal border/custody; absence of data is not safety.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.25-C has birth-sex prison placement and cross-dressing arrests; this division has identity-consistent custody and no criminal facilities law, raising it, but federal border/custody severity keeps it in Elevated Risk.

0.35-A is routine visitor exclusion without custody; our visa/screening exposure is severe but not universal reporting, and state shield/anti-discrimination protections push above it despite federal custody abuse.

0.55-B is extended secondary screening with administrative denial; similar border friction, but this regime adds documented immigration custody abuse and counterterrorism framing, partly offset by strong state protections.

0.65-A shows brief friction with working remedy and no plausible imprisonment; here federal document refusal, fraud ineligibility, and custody outcomes are harsher, so the combined regime rates below despite state protections.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is split. At border, national passport/visa birth-sex rules, mismatch screening, fraud ineligibility and possible removal/stranding are traveler-facing and severe. If a traveller is referred into federal immigration or national corrections custody, documented abuse, forced labour, sexual violence, and conversion-therapy policies raise consequences materially. The protective state layer substantially reduces everyday state-level risk: public accommodations, identity documents, anti-hate-crime machinery, shield law for care, custody consistency and school protections help adults and travelling minors, especially those fleeing home-state bans. It does not erase federal entry screening or federal facilities, and the national counterterrorism/minors-care framing leaves uncertainty. Adult alone and guardian with minor are safer in-state than the national average but remain exposed at entry and any federal encounter.
